content:
Thirty-four years ago, Sharon Stone became a sex symbol thanks to her passionate performance in Basic Instinct, and now she says she has accepted being single.

This week Stone appeared on Mayim Bialik's "Breakdown" podcast for a wide-ranging interview, revealing that she hasn't been in a relationship for a long time because her love life has recently been "completely fruitless."

The Oscar-nominated actress said: "I've been single for quite a long time." She added that she has "reached a stage where I really only want to be with someone I love."

Stone's three sons — 26-year-old Roan, 21-year-old Laird, and 20-year-old Quinn — have grown up, and she feels her priorities regarding romance have changed.

She said: "I want a partner, not just someone to sleep with. I'm a bit tired of that kind of relationship. So I'm at a stage of 'completely fruitless,' but I think this is a stage you have to be willing to get to in order to have what I truly want."

Stone was married to journalist Phil Bronstein for six years, and the two had their eldest son Roan. They divorced in 2004. Before that, she was married to television and film producer Michael Greenburg from 1984 to 1987.

In 2018, media reports said she was dating actor and producer Angelo Boffa, who has Italian and Swiss heritage. The two reportedly split later that same year.

Elsewhere in her "Breakdown" interview, Stone said she didn't think she had "experienced the greatest love of her life," and mentioned speaking to a psychic, who told her she would meet her life partner at "quite an advanced age, almost 70."

The 68-year-old quipped: "Well, now would be the time."

Stone is one of a growing number of celebrities speaking openly about choosing to live a celibate life. In 2024, musician Lenny Kravitz revealed he had not had sex for nine years, while actress Julia Fox said the Supreme Court's 2022 overturning of abortion rights prompted her to become celibate.

This February, former Project Runway mentor Tim Gunn, who appeared on Chelsea Handler's "Dear Chelsea" podcast, shared that he had been celibate for 43 years since breaking up with a cheating ex in 1982.

He said this lifestyle prepared him to cope with the extended self-isolation brought by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020: "I might be one of the few people who actually enjoyed that period."
